messages.author: 6cf4f730b8d1254e
messages.subject: Zero-truncated poisson lognormal
parts:
Hello all,

I'm attempting to fit the model from Engen et al. 2011 ("Estimating similarity of communities: a parametric approach to spatio-temporal analysis of species diversity"), who employ a zero-truncated poisson lognormal distribution to estimate the similarity between two communities, when the sampling intensity is unknown.

Unfortunately, the optimizer is unable to evaluate the function returned by TMB at the (true) starting values, so I suspect there is an issue with either my code, or the combination of the model and the laplace approximation.

Any feedback, suggestions or improvements are greatly appreciated.

TMB-code
#include <TMB.hpp>
#include<math.h>

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
{
  DATA_MATRIX(y);
 
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(u);
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(rho);
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(lg_sigma);
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(mu);
 
  vector <Type> sigma = exp(lg_sigma);
 
  int n = y.cols();
  int p = y.rows();
 
  using namespace density;
  Type nll = 0.0;

  for (int j=0; j<p;j++){
        Type q = 1.0;
        Type q0 = 1.0;
        for (int i=0; i<n;i++){  
         q *= (exp(u(i)*sigma(i)*y(j,i)+mu(i)*y(j,i)-exp(-(u(i)*sigma(i)+mu(i))))/exp(lfactorial(y(j,i))));
         q0 *= exp(-exp(-(u(i)*sigma(i)+mu(i))));  
        }
        q *= exp(-1*UNSTRUCTURED_CORR(rho)(u));
        q0 *= exp(-1*UNSTRUCTURED_CORR(rho)(u));
       
    nll -= log(q/(1-q0));
  }

  REPORT(UNSTRUCTURED_CORR(rho).cov());
 
  return nll;
 
}

R-code
library(poilog)

y <- rbipoilog(S=100, mu1=1, mu2=2, sig1=1, sig2=2, rho=0.7, nu1=0.5, nu2=0.7)
sigma <- c(1, 2)
mu<-c(1, 2)
rho <- 0.7
u <- c(0.5, 0.7)

library(TMB)
compile(file="TMB.cpp")

dyn.load(dynlib("TMB"))
objr <- MakeADFun(
  data = list(y = y),
  parameters = list(u=u, rho=rho, lg_sigma=log(sigma), mu=mu),
  DLL = "TMB",
  random="u")

opt<-optim(objr$par,objr$fn,objr$gr,method="BFGS")

dyn.unload(dynlib("TMB"))

Bert

parts:
I haven't looked at this carefully at all, but (1) I would strongly
recommend doing the calculations in the log-space as far as possible,
*then* exponentiating (use logspace_add and logspace_sub where possible,
see e.g.
https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/group__special__functions.html#ga2d5a07f1202dc628ba18ee9a2af8b9cd
and (2) I'm not sure of the detailed form of this, but it might be
possible to implement in glmmTMB using an observation-level random effect?

messages.author: 16c32bb3268768fd
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Zero-truncated poisson lognormal
parts: I agree with Ben that you should look into using a Poisson distribution with observation-level random effect. I've been able to generate data using the poilog package in R (from Engen et al. 2002) which results in comparable likelihoods calculated from dpoilog and TMB using a Poisson with an observation-level random effect. The TMB model can easily be extended to treat the random effects as arriving from a spatial-temporal process.
